Lane 1 (per-epoch index builds) is approved and recorded in the decision log. What remains is the backfill design: how each historical source gets processed through the librarian — order is proposed below, but the per-source processes (extractor, batching, corroboration behavior on old material) still need real design work, detailed row by row in the migration map.
Proposed order: Discord → past PRs → worker history.

Discord first because it is smallest and purest: the archive is already distilled, attributed notes (37 Markdown files, ~1 MB, 328 indexed chunks) — a short librarian pass, not a chat-log crawl. Past PRs second: 2,730 complete folders with postmortems, diffs, and
already linking PRs to files. Worker history third: 3,987 worker_state rows and 12.5k checkpoints.

Transcripts only cover part of the history (2,870 files, June 7–15 window); everything else backfills from checkpoints, summaries, and activity timelines — consistent with the checkpoints-are-the-substrate decision. Transcript-grounded condensation applies where transcripts exist and to everything going forward.
Two doors per source, one per backfill.
The Discord daily cron (forward door) consumes raw messages later; the backfill door consumes the existing distillate now. Data sheet and external mirrors stay parked per the retirement decisions.

Framing resolved: present-anchored backfill + Discord repull are decided, and the process is detailed (with canvas) in the migration map. What remains per source: PR batching strategy, worker-history scope (how far back checkpoints alone are worth condensing), and the Discord CLI tool choice.
